tool.name: FASTA collection concat
tool.description: concatenate all FASTAs in a list collection into a single multifasta
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/fasta_concat.py' #if $compressed --gzip --output '$output_gz' #else --output '$output' #end if #for $f in $inputs# '$f' #end for# ## ⛔ VERIFY THE GZIP TRAILER. gzip stores CRC32 and the uncompressed length in the last 8 ## bytes, so `gzip -t` is a complete integrity test, not a header sniff: a write that stopped ## early fails it. Galaxy cannot do this declaratively -- <assert_contents> exists only inside ## <tests>, so it never runs on a production job -- and a truncated .gz still sniffs as ## fasta.gz and still reports ok. detect_errors="aggressive" turns the non-zero exit into a ## failed job. #if $compressed && gzip -t '$output_gz' #end if

param.name: inputs
param.label: FASTAs to concatenate
param.help: Order is preserved from collection order.

tool.help:
**FASTA collection concat** — concatenate every FASTA in the input collection into a single multifasta. Order matches collection order.
Handles plain `.fasta` and `.fasta.gz` inputs transparently — decompresses .gz inputs when needed.
Useful in pangenome workflows after per-strain PanSN renaming, before piping into `pggb`. The IUC `fasta-merge` tool covers most cases; this exists because pggb specifically wants a single bgzip-compatible multifasta and our pansn_rename outputs are per-strain.
